digest.component_or_area: Git operation outcome classification and retry policy
propositions: Five sites classify git failure strings with different verdicts for identical text; a single registry keyed by (marker, operation) pair disambiguates the classification and preserves intentional divergence for 'cannot lock ref' which legitimately means retriable local lock, a non-lease push reject, or held advisory lock depending on operation context.

The synthetic timeout result (rc-124 'git timed out after') is constructed in four places with inconsistent retry application; consolidating construction into one shared run_git_bounded function and registering its outcome as TRANSIENT_FS enables consistent retry across sync._union_merge, push_recovery, and other callsites.

The ten GitOutcome kinds (LOCK, TRANSIENT_FS, TRANSPORT, NON_FF, CAS_MISMATCH, POLICY_DECLINE, DIRTY_WD, UNMERGED, INVALID_OBJECT, FATAL) are mutually exclusive verdicts over failure strings and structural predicates; policy-decline rule subtracts from non-fast-forward to preserve bug-fix semantics from 4afc and ebee.

The registry admits two entry kinds: marker-row mappings for common cases and structural predicates run first per-operation for shape-dependent verdicts like _is_cas_mismatch, which discriminates on command arguments and exit codes that no (marker, operation) table can express.

Guard A (text literal analysis over src/rebar/_store and _engine/rebar_reconciler) proves marker strings live only in git_outcome.py owner module except two reasoned escapes: _LOCK_REF_RE parsing and _reclaim_if_stale_index_lock path joining; Guard B (AST conjunction over src/rebar/_store) proves the synthetic timeout construction exists only once in gitutil.run_git_bounded, not in the three shims.

INVALID_OBJECT is a distinct tenth kind with a rebuild-then-retry recovery action for write-tree failures referencing missing objects, separate from FATAL to preserve its index-recovery handler in event_append.py.
